questions.prompt: How are ordinary objects compared with ===?
options: All empty object literals compare equal.
By reference identity, not by recursively comparing their properties.
By comparing every nested property automatically.
By comparing the order in which keys were declared.
questions.explanation: Two separately created object literals are different objects even if their properties look identical.

questions.prompt: What should you remember about spread syntax on an object with nested objects?
options: It always performs a deep clone.
It serializes the object to JSON.
The copy is shallow; nested object references can still be shared.
questions.explanation: Spread copies enumerable own properties one level deep, so nested objects may still be aliased.
